summary: 1939 International Derrick steel fire lookout on Warner Hill, Derry NH; WWII aircraft watch; state-owned and active; access sources conflict.

facts.design: Steel International Derrick tower, six tiers, with a cab added in 1979 that raised it; original height 41 feet

staffing.status: conflicting: register lists unstaffed; Derry News describes a watchman and closure except on the most dangerous fire days

access.note: State-owned active fire tower. Register lists no signs and no staffing; Derry News says the state has closed the tower except on the most dangerous fire days but visitors can still climb to the top landing; NH Family Hikes says it is seldom visited. Check with the Division before visiting.

visit.trail_note: NH Family Hikes gives directions; Wardens Way leads 0.1 miles up to the fire tower. Public access is disputed, so check first.

events.note: Commissioned 1939 per register; Forest Lookouts says erected 1938-39; federal emergency funds and CCC labor
Arthur Picard hired April 22, 1939 to watch from the hilltop until the tower was ready; made permanent observer after opening in early July 1939
Used as an aircraft warning service station in the early 1940s
Army left the aircraft warning station; state bought the two acres from the Mears family for $400
Roscoe Smith took over as watchman starting in the 1950s
Sixth tier added and cab raised
Walter Eaton took the watchman post around 1985
Bids advertised February 2015; current cab built 2015 during an extensive restoration
May 2017 photo shows walls removed from the lower cab; register says the tower is being remodeled

corrections.proposed: 184 (Derry News crest, 605 ft); register value 388 ft (118 m) reported as a conflict
corrections.why: The brief's 118.3 m matches the register's 388 ft (118 m), so the brief value is a register figure, not an error. Derry News gives the crest as 605 feet (about 184 m) and the Derry historic survey gives 604 feet. The story uses the Derry News figure and reports the register's figure as a conflict.

corrections.current: NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development
corrections.why: Not a brief error. The register's 'Administered by' field names NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development, with NH Div. of Forests and Lands as cooperator. Historic Structures says the state owns and operates the tower through the Division. The story names only the Division, which both sources support.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says commissioned 1939; Forest Lookouts says erected 1938-39; Historic Structures says completed for the 1939 season; Derry historic survey says c. 1935, which no other source supports. Story uses 1938-39 construction with a 1939 first season.
Historic Structures gives 41 feet as the original height; Derry News recalls about 55 feet when opened. Not resolved; the story reports both.
Register gives 388 ft (118 m). Derry News gives the crest as 605 feet; the Derry historic survey gives 604 feet. The story uses the Derry News figure and reports the register's figure.

notes_for_editor: Elevation conflict: the register's 388 ft (118 m) matches the brief's 118.3 m; the crest figures are 605 ft (Derry News) and 604 ft (Derry survey). The story reports the Derry News figure and the register's figure. Agency: the department name the brief used is on the register, so it was not an error; the story names only the Division of Forests & Lands. Access and staffing conflict: the register says unstaffed with no signs; Derry News says a watchman has served since about 1985 and the tower is closed except on the most dangerous fire days, though the top landing is climbable. Check with the Division of Forests & Lands before publishing access wording. The 1935 survey date is an outlier. The Derry News column is undated; its 75th-anniversary remark points to about 2014. Historic Structures gives both a leased 1-acre tract and a 2-acre purchase for the Mears land; the story uses the 2-acre figure from the quote. No photos recorded.
